The document doesn't contain most of the items you asked for. It doesn't mention an ambient code (a3b2 or a6b1), vfast/vslow, ambient density or temperature rules, Br scaling, an alpha fraction, ENLIL 2.7/2.8, WSA 2.2, or gamma. It also doesn't give a journal, volume, or page. What it does cover is below.

**Inner boundary and CME cloud settings**

- The CME is inserted as "a time-dependent inner boundary condition at 21.5 solar radii" (Section 2).
- The CME cloud density is "is a free parameter which by default is 4 times larger than typical mean values in the ambient fast wind" (Section 2). Paraphrased, the default gives a CME pressure four times that of the ambient fast wind.
- "The cloud temperature is taken to be equal to the ambient fast wind temperature." (Section 2)
- The cavity ratio defaults to no cavity (radcav = 0) (Section 2).

**Ambient solar wind settings**

- The WSA coronal map supplies the magnetic field and solar wind speed at the coronal-heliospheric boundary, usually at 21.5 solar radii, and is generated from synoptic magnetograms (Section 2).
- The ambient speed reduction factor is described as one that "reduces the solar wind speed provided by the WSA coronal map" (Section 7). Its default is 25 km/s (Section 7).
- The base ensemble's modeled background speed was about 125 km/s higher than observed in situ (Section 7).

**Bibliographic information**

- **Title:** "Ensemble modeling of CMEs using the WSA-ENLIL+Cone model"
- **Authors:** M.L. Mays, A. Taktakishvili, A. Pulkkinen, P.J. MacNeice, L. Rastätter, D. Odstrcil, L.K. Jian, I.G. Richardson, J.A. LaSota, Y. Zheng, M.M. Kuznetsova
- **Journal, volume, page:** Not stated. The page header identifies the source as arXiv:1504.04402.

**Title:** "Verification of real-time WSA–ENLIL+Cone simulations of CME arrival-time at the CCMC from 2010–2016"

**Authors (as listed):** Alexandra M. Wold, M. Leila Mays, A. Taktakishvili, L. K. Jian, D. Odstrcil, P. MacNeice, and others with affiliations.

**Journal, volume, article number:** Not in the page. The only identifier is the arXiv ID, 1801.07818.

**ENLIL/WSA versions and ambient settings**
- The main runs used ENLIL version 2.7 with ambient setting "a4b1" and WSA version 2.2.
- Earlier runs used an earlier ENLIL version 2.6 with ambient setting "a3b2".

**Inner boundary and CME insertion**
- WSA approximates solar wind outflow at 21.5 R⊙, beyond the solar wind critical point.
- A CME can be inserted at the inner boundary of 21.5 R⊙.
- CMEs are inserted "as slices of a homogeneous spherical plasma cloud with uniform velocity, density, and temperature."
- This is a time-dependent inner boundary condition with a "steady magnetic field."

**Cone model**
- The Cone model "assumes isotropic expansion, radial propagation, and constant CME cone angular width."

**Other ENLIL parameters (discussion section)**
- Reducing "the ENLIL model parameter of CME cloud density ratio" may help predict later arrivals.
- The cavity ratio is the radial CME cavity width divided by the CME width.

**Not in the provided content:** The page does not mention momentum flux or thermal pressure balance rules, fast wind density or temperature values, velocity reduction, Br, or Cone model defaults for density (4x) or temperature.

The search turned up the core ENLIL inner-boundary scheme, though not a source that ties it directly to Odstrcil's Br-scaling specifically.

- **Density and temperature are derived, not given.** The WSA radial field and velocity set the boundary, and ENLIL then computes density and temperature. One source says the density comes from constant momentum flux, while the temperature is set so thermal pressure balances at the boundary (ENLIL uses values of the radial solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field components provided by the WSA coronal model and calculates the density and temperature assuming constant momentum flux and pressure at the inner boundary at 21.5 Rs.).
- **Momentum-flux form.** A 2021 arXiv paper writes the constraint at 0.1 AU as N·v_r² equal to a constant, with the constant expressed through free parameters d_fast and v_fast. It notes these can be tuned to observations, or applied afterward by scaling the solution (the condition of constant momentum flux holds: N_e v_r² = d_fast · v_fast² = const, with d_fast and v_fast as free parameters).
- **Scaling.** The same paper suggests that if precision isn't critical, you can scale the density solution directly after the run. It also argues that choosing v_fast from the WSA velocity distribution gives near-constant average density at 1 AU, after which d_fast can be scaled to OMNI density.
- **Temperature is the weak point.** A 2025 ensemble study found that temperature was the least reliably reconstructed of the boundary variables, and suggested improving how temperature is derived from radial velocity and density.
- **Fast wind and thermal pressure.** An extended MHD review notes that the observed fast solar wind (speed 700–800 km/s) cannot be produced by thermal pressure without temperatures greatly exceeding coronal values. This is the physical reason ENLIL's fast-wind boundary needs the momentum-flux treatment rather than a purely thermal source.
- **Odstrcil and Br.** The Odstrcil (2003) reference appears only as the citation for ENLIL's general model description. The search did not return a source on Br scaling in the Odstrcil formulation, so that part of your query is unconfirmed.

**Citation:** "Operational Modeling of Heliospheric Space Weather for the *Parker Solar Probe*," by Dusan Odstrcil, M. Leila Mays, Phillip Hess, Shaela I. Jones, Carl J. Henney, and Charles N. Arge. *The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series*, Volume 246, Number 2, Article 73 (2020). DOI: 10.3847/1538-4365/ab77cb.

The visible text does not contain the parameter names you listed (bfast, bscl, vfast, dfast, tfast), so I can't map them directly. The closest matching passages are below.

**Inner boundary prescriptions (at 21.5 Rs, 0.1 au)**

- **Velocity from WSA:** "ENLIL uses values of the radial solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field components provided by the WSA coronal model." The paper also notes that the meridional and azimuthal velocities are set to zero.
- **Density:** The density is derived from velocity. "the solar wind density is a derived quantity calculated from the solar wind radial velocity." The paper gives the relation N ∝ 1/V² in an embedded equation.
- **Temperature (thermal pressure):** "the temperature is chosen to assure thermal balance on the source surface, the inner heliospheric boundary at 21.5 Rs."
- **Br scaling and azimuthal field:** "the magnetic field scaling factor (default of four for GONG inputs)." Bφ is set from Br, sin θ, and the ratio V_rot/V_r, where V_rot corresponds to the 27.2753-day rotation period. The formula is embedded as an image, so it is not reproduced in text.
- **Alpha fraction:** The model-free parameters include "the fraction of alpha particles," along with the ambient wind parameters that are tuned against observations (this paper uses a7b1).
- **Gamma and heating:** The paper first notes "The ratio of specific heats, γ = 1.5 crudely reflects nonideal processes in the solar wind." It then adds volumetric heating so that "allows us to keep γ = 5/3 and provide the radial decrease of temperature as 1/r."

**Fast-stream reference values (0.1 au)**

- The paper gives the reference fast-wind values as "N = 200 cm−3, temperature, T = 1 MK, and radial velocity Vr = 700 km s−1." These are the closest match to the vfast, dfast, and tfast values you asked for.

**CME (Cone) defaults**

- The Cone model assumes "a constant angular width of CMEs observed in coronagraphs."
- The cloud has "a uniform velocity (corresponding the fitted CME speed)."
- Density is "four times larger than the mean density in the fast stream."
- Temperature is "equal to the mean temperature in the fast stream."
- For ellipsoidal ejecta, "The ellipsoidal shape has the major radius as the spherical shape and the minor radius is half of this width."
- Zero tilt is used for all ellipsoidal ejecta, because the HCS is basically flat in the simulated period.

The source text was truncated, so some later sections may contain additional parameter definitions I could not see.

I didn't find the specific CCMC run page for "a6b1," and no result confirms a 2024 or 2025 run with a WSA "tfast" setting. The closest relevant hit is a 2025 NASA/NOAA annex report on CME arrival-time modeling, which is useful context for the parameters you named.

- **Parameter handling:** The report notes that the ENLIL versions differ in how vfast, bfast, dfast, and tfast are used for scaling and/or clipping WSA values, which could matter when comparing runs.
- **Default boundary setting:** It also says that the general default value of bscl for GONG-driven WSA-ENLIL simulations installed at CCMC is bscl=4 or 5, and that a possible miscommunication led to using bscl=1 in SWPC operations.
- **Fast-stream defaults:** A 2010 CCMC workshop slide lists the defaults for these fast-stream inputs, including a temperature of 150 for the fast stream, but the extracted text does not clearly map each value to its parameter name, so I wouldn't rely on that number without checking the slide.
- **Run pages:** CCMC run results are reached through URLs of the form https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/results/viewrun.php?domain=SH&runnumber=, with a run name in place of the placeholder. A run named "a6b1" would presumably follow that pattern, but I could not confirm it exists.

To find the run itself, the CCMC Runs-on-Request results pages or the NASA/NOAA annex report's appendix (which may list run IDs) are the best next places to check.

The excerpt I was given doesn't include the items you asked for: the WSA velocity equation and coefficients, Table 3's vrfast/vrslow values, the qheat/heating codes, the cone cloud defaults, or the a6b1/a8b1 definitions. It begins partway through the Conclusions and runs through the reference list, supplemental tables (5–9), and figure captions (12–18).

The excerpt does label several configurations, which may help you locate the right section:

- Table 5 is for "GONG WSA 2.2 ENLIL 2.6.2 a3b2."
- Table 6 is for "GONG WSA 2.2 ENLIL 2.9e a8b1."
- Tables 7 and 8 use "GONGz WSA 4.5" with ENLIL 2.6.2 a3b2 and ENLIL 2.9e a8b1, respectively.
- Table 9 is for "GONGz ADAPT WSA 4.5 ENLIL 2.9e a8b1 (median)."

The definitions and parameter values are probably in the Models (Section II) and Methodology (Section III) sections, which fall before the 100,000-character offset. If you can share that portion, I can pull out the exact wording, keeping quotes under 125 characters.

I can't reproduce all of Table 3 verbatim, but here is what the text supports.

**WSA velocity coefficients:** The only related sentence in the excerpt is that "WSA version 4.5 uses different coefficients in the velocity equation" (Section V.4). The excerpt does not give the coefficient values.

**NOAA operational WSA-Enlil v3.0 (WSA 5.4 + Enlil 2.9e):** The excerpt doesn't mention this configuration. The text describes the operational setup as ENLIL 2.9e with WSA 2.2 (after May 2019), not v3.0 or WSA 5.4.

**Cone parameters (cloud density ratio, temperature, radcav):** These don't appear in the excerpt. The content was also truncated, so they may be in the omitted portion.

**Table 3 (ENLIL 2.9e settings), summarized:** Column 2 (a3b2) replicates v2.6.2, and column 3 (a8b1) uses the v2.9e defaults. Key differences include:
- **Ambient wind:** The a8b1 column uses a higher fast-stream B-field (bfast 500 vs. 300), a non-zero slow-stream and mean-stream B-field, and a higher fast-stream speed (vfast 700 vs. 675).
- **Magnetic scaling:** bscl is 5 for a8b1 and 1 for a3b2.
- **Heating:** Heating is off for a3b2 and on for a8b1 (qheat 100000, nheat 2).
- **Time settings:** The a8b1 column uses a 120 h output step and a shorter start-up (tstart -180 h vs. -360 h).
- **Coronal mode:** a3b2 uses cormode=single; a8b1 uses single/multi.

For the exact values of every row, see Table 3 in the arXiv PDF (arXiv:2512.14462v1).
